newsitem.title: UK: Oil rallies as product stocks fall in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Oil rallies as product stocks fall in U.S.

text.p: World oil prices rose on Wednesday in response to mildly bullish stock data from the United States.
The modest recovery from a series of seven consecutive days' losses was seen by some traders as heralding a period of relative stability for the market.
At 1600 GMT benchmark December Brent crude was trading 18 cents higher at $22.37 a barrel on the London futures market.
"I think we might find some stability this week," said Russel Hill, senior trader at Austrian oil company OMV.
"Short term the market looks a little oversupplied ...but generally demand is buoyant," he added.
Both the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Energy Information Administration (EIA) reported a surprise drop in U.S. distillate stocks in the week ending November 1.
They also showed crude stocks rose quite sharply, but the market preferred to focus on downstream products.

EIA data released on Wednedsay showed U.S. distillate stocks fell 500,000 barrels last week and the API data, issued after the market close on Tuesday, pegged the drop at 429,000. Analysts had expected a build of some 2.5 million barrels.
Within the distillate category, key heating oil inventories in fact rose - but by less than dealers had expected, helping to underpin heating oil oil and crude values.
Traders also noted that heating oil stocks were still well down on year-ago levels.

Low heating oil stocks in the run-up to the peak northern hemisphere winter demand period were one of the main factors behind the blistering rally in oil to a six-year peak of $25.06 per barrel in mid-October.
But mild weather, a recovery in heating oil stocks and investment fund selling helped wipe over 10 percent off the price of a barrel of oil.
While another cold snap would aid any recovery, the highs may not be broken for some time, some analysts said.
"I am fairly friendly to this market, but I am less confident of taking out the 1996 high this year," Hill said.
